Words I like;
"If you can't measure it, you can't improve it." Peter Drucker said that about business, but it works for your wallet too.
Here's the math most people never do: one 24-pack of bottled water runs about $6 these days. If your family goes through two packs a week (pretty normal for a household of four), that's $624 a year. Over five years? $3,120. Over ten? $6,240.

# COMPETITIVE INTEL BRIEF — Week of May 5, 2026

## Executive Summary

The competitive landscape remains stable with no dramatic shifts this week. Mermaid Water continues aggressive promotion bundling across plumbing and water treatment in Manassas, running four simultaneous offers including $200 water heater discounts and free Kinetico installation. EcoWater and Hampton Roads maintain their existing positioning with no detectable changes. The biggest opportunity gap: none of these players are leading with outcome-driven messaging or commercial differentiation—they're stuck on features and free tests.

## Per-Competitor Intelligence

| Competitor | Hero positioning | Distinct services | Pricing visible? | Notable shift this week |
|------------|-----------------|-------------------|------------------|------------------------|
| **Mermaid Water** (local, Manassas) | "Get clean, healthy water and dependable plumbing from a local team" | Plumbing + water treatment bundle; Kinetico authorized dealer; pump systems; commercial DI resin systems | Yes — $200 water heater discount, $100 new customer, free Kinetico install on whole-home, free heater flush with softener | None detected |
| **EcoWater** (national franchise) | "Premier Water Softener, Filtration and Treatment Systems — Better Water Starts Here" | Smart home leak detection; conservation tech; symptom-based product finder ("if you have scale...") | No | None detected |
| **Hampton Roads Water Services** (local, Tidewater/Richmond) | "Your Full Service Water Quality Experts" | Annual water testing programs; lifetime warranty emphasis; "Made in USA" systems from Chicago factory | No (free test only) | None detected |

## Implications for ClearWave

- **Test commercial messaging hard.** Mermaid mentions commercial services but buries them; Hampton Roads and EcoWater ignore B2B entirely. If ClearWave can own "commercial water treatment in Virginia" on paid search and homepage, there's white space.
- **Consider a structured promotion calendar.** Mermaid is running four offers simultaneously—likely eroding margin and confusing buyers. ClearWave should test *one* clear, time-bound offer per month with urgency mechanics.
- **Lead with outcomes, not equipment.** All three competitors default to "free water test" + product catalog. Test hero copy focused on business continuity, regulatory compliance, or home resale value instead of "clean water."

## Watch Items

- **Mermaid's promotion fatigue** — track whether they rotate or stack offers next week; if stacking continues, they may be struggling with pipeline.
- **EcoWater's "smart home" push** — leak detection and conservation tech could appeal to higher-end residential; monitor for local dealer activation.
- **Hampton Roads' lifetime warranty** — claims "industry's most comprehensive" but details hidden; get a quote to reverse-engineer their service model and margin structure.
